No breakups, nobody died, I didn't buy a house or get a dog or anything like that. It's just... steady. My personal life is completely steady. 

And honestly, I think that's why this whole thing at the county is driving me up the wall. Because everything else in my life is so normal, so predictable, and then I have to walk into that office and deal with this... this absolute madness. If I had some crazy personal drama going on, maybe I wouldn't be so focused on the paperwork, but I don't. I just go to work, I do my job—my award-winning job, like I said—and I come home. 

But now, when I come home, all I can do is sit there in my quiet apartment and replay those emails in my head. I sit there thinking about how they're twisting my reports, trying to figure out what their next move is. Because why would I be distracted by anything else when my entire career, everything I've built since I was eighteen, is being systematically dismantled by my own department? So, no, doctor, nothing outside of work. Work is the only thing that's changed, and it's only changed because they decided to coordinate this whole thing against me.

========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Voices? Like, hearing things that aren't there? No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I know that's one of those standard questions you guys have to ask, like checking the boxes on a mental health form, right? Just like when I do a suspension check, I have to check the box for the strut mounts even if I know they're fine. It's standard procedure. But no, I don't hear voices or sounds or anything out of the ordinary. 

Honestly, the only voices I hear are the ones in the office, and those are very real, believe me. I hear them whispering by the coffee machine when I walk in. I hear the way they suddenly stop talking when I pass by the breakroom. And it's not like I'm imagining it—you can literally feel the shift in the room. But actual, like, hallucinations? No. My hearing is perfectly fine. In fact, you have to have excellent hearing to do my job. When you're under a county bus checking the air brakes, you have to be able to listen for the tiniest hiss of a leak. If you can't hear that, you miss a failing valve, and then you've got a multi-ton vehicle on the road with compromised stopping power. So, my ears are sharp. Very sharp. 

But as far as hearing things that other people can't? Absolutely not. I'm completely grounded in reality. That's the whole problem here, doctor. I'm too grounded in reality. I see and hear exactly what's going on around me, and I'm the only one willing to call it out. If I was hearing voices, maybe they could use that against me, you know? They could put that in my file and say, 'Oh, he's losing it, we have to let him go.' But they can't do that, because my mind is perfectly clear. I don't hear voices, I don't see things, I just read the emails they send and listen to the real, actual words they say when they're trying to build this case against me.

An exaggeration? A distortion? Doc, listen to me... I know how it sounds. If I were sitting in your chair and some guy came in off the street saying all this, maybe I’d ask the same thing. In fact, you have to have excellent hearing to do my job. When you're under a county bus checking the air brakes, you have to be able to listen for the tiniest hiss of a leak. If you can't hear that, you miss a failing valve, and then you've got a multi-ton vehicle on the road with compromised stopping power. So, my ears are sharp. I see and hear exactly what's going on around me, and I'm the only one willing to call it out. If I was hearing voices, maybe they could use that against me, you know? Change my mind? Well, doctor, look... it’s not about changing my mind like we’re arguing over who's going to win the Super Bowl or what the best brand of motor oil is. It’s not an opinion. It's not a feeling I just woke up with one day.
